# Kaspa

> Kaspa is a fair-launched proof-of-work blockDAG cryptocurrency running at 10 blocks per second, built for real-time decentralization.

English content generated from the website during the build. External resources are linked, not copied.

## Developer resources

- [Kaspa documentation](https://docs.kaspa.org): Developer guides and protocol documentation.
- [WASM SDK documentation](https://kaspa.aspectron.org/docs/): Browser and Node.js bindings for applications, wallets, and RPC access.
- [Rusty Kaspa](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa): Core node, native Rust libraries, wallet and RPC implementation.
- [Developer tools and SDK documentation](https://kaspa.org/build): WASM SDK, node access, and separately labelled community tools.
- [Community REST API](https://api.kaspa.org/docs): Community-operated Kaspa REST API. Best-effort, no SLA or guaranteed availability. Integrators who depend on it should run their own instance.
- [REST API source and self-hosting](https://github.com/kaspa-ng/kaspa-rest-server): Upstream contacts: lAmeR1 / supertypo.
- [API catalog](https://kaspa.org/.well-known/api-catalog): Machine-readable directory of listed APIs.

# Kaspa | Proof-of-Work blockDAG for Real-Time Decentralization

Source: https://kaspa.org/

Kaspa is a fair-launched proof-of-work blockDAG cryptocurrency running at 10 blocks per second, built for real-time decentralization.

# Real-time
Decentralization

bitcoin's proof-of-work without the wait.

[Get started](https://kaspa.org/lore) [Get a wallet](https://kaspa.org/hodl#wallet) [Buy Kaspa](https://kaspa.org/hodl#buy)

Every coin in Kaspa's history traces cryptographically back to an empty genesis.

No premine. No hidden allocation. Fair launch.

The genesis proof follows the chain of pruning-point block hashes backward to the original genesis and verifies its UTXO commitment matches an empty set. Bitcoin block hashes embedded in the genesis coinbase serve as timestamps, ruling out hidden premining.

[Run the proof](https://github.com/kaspagang/kaspad-py-explorer/blob/main/src/genesis_proof.ipynb)

---

# LORE | Kaspa

Source: https://kaspa.org/lore

Kaspa is a fair-launched proof-of-work blockDAG focused on real-time decentralization, with no premine, no insider allocation, and 10 BPS mainnet performance.

# Kaspa is a live proof-of-work blockDAG running at 10 blocks per second.

## The shift

It takes a different route from older proof-of-work chains. Parallel blocks are not discarded. They are ordered. Many of the limits associated with proof of work came from older chain architecture, not from proof of work itself. [PHANTOM / GHOSTDAG paper](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/104.pdf)

## Brief history

Kaspa grew out of blockDAG research at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and later Harvard. The research line dates back to the [GHOST protocol section of the Ethereum white paper](https://ethereum.org/en/whitepaper/#modified-ghost-implementation), surfaced early through the Bitcoin research circuit, and continued through SPECTRE and PHANTOM into the protocols running Kaspa today. [Scaling Bitcoin 2015](https://youtu.be/8IlZ80mPWfE?si=metsyYxZ8pnBgRMf&t=1583) · [CoinDesk, 2017](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2017/10/25/spectre-creators-seek-vc-backing-for-blockchain-free-cryptocurrency)

Mainnet launched in November 2021 as a fair-launched proof-of-work network. No premine, insider allocation, or pre-sales. Every coin in circulation has been mined in the open from genesis onward. That fair launch gave Kaspa a broad and loyal community. That remains one of its strongest achievements and one of its core strengths. [Launch plan](https://hashdag.medium.com/kaspa-launch-plan-responding-to-reality-6b4bec449037) · [Genesis proof](https://github.com/kaspagang/kaspad-py-explorer/blob/main/src/genesis_proof.ipynb)

## North star

Real-time decentralization is Kaspa's north star.

Real-time is a non-compromise. Impatience is Kaspa's primitive instinct - a tantrum against wait times, rejecting limits the adults just accept. And we demand this not only for speed but for the hardcore Satoshi properties as well - censorship resistance, permissionless settlement, competitive mining - all achieved in real time, not eventually. This is not achievable in real time without proof of work. [PoW uniqueness](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/1973887808776675365)

Kaspa achieving RTD means the protocol samples the honest majority of the mining network in every consensus round. This allows transactions that confirm safely after an hour in Bitcoin to confirm in seconds on Kaspa; or it guarantees that Kaspa achieves censorship resistance within seconds - what takes an hour in Bitcoin. This matters not only for settlement speed but for every context where real-time sequencing is critical - market resolutions, liquidation cascades, anywhere a single consensus leader ordering transactions at its own discretion grants them too much power.

Real-time sampling of the honest majority can also be utilized to achieve a trustless real-time data and event feed governed by the mining network. [RTD post](https://hashdag.medium.com/in-which-it-was-never-my-choice-to-hold-the-fire-we-found-937314149402)

RTD has also a defensive side. Partial synchrony (with the upcoming DAGKnight) protocols uniquely implement the dual property of being fast when the network is healthy and slow-yet-secure when it is not. Kaspa sells speed to normies and wargrade money to cypherpunks.

* * *

## Shipped and next

The original Golang node was rewritten from scratch in Rust. The rewrite was backed by a 100M KAS community grant and turned into a real open-source effort around _rusty-kaspa_, with a broad contributor base. [Rusty Kaspa GitHub](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa)

That rewrite is what made Crescendo possible. Kaspa could not move to 10 blocks per second on mainnet without it. Crescendo is where the thesis became live. [Crescendo reference](https://medium.com/@michaelsuttonil/unveiling-the-crescendo-hard-fork-roadmap-10bps-and-more-6072329e177f) · [Release notes](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/releases/tag/v1.0.0)

[View Rusty Kaspa contributors on GitHub+30 contributors](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/graphs/contributors)

* * *

### Toccata hardfork

Toccata activated on mainnet on June 30, 2026, at DAA score 474,165,565. Programmability on L1. Covenants -- the construction coined by Gregory Maxwell in a 2013 BitcoinTalk post -- are spending rules that carry state forward across transactions. They restrict who can spend and how. This is what programmability means in a UTXO-principled, verification-oriented environment like Bitcoin or Kaspa. Covenants open the way to vaults, smart wallets, and native assets. [BitcoinTalk, 2013](https://bitcointalk.org/index.php?topic=278122.msg2970937#msg2970937)

Toccata is a ground-up design of OP\_CAT, the heatedly debated Bitcoin opcode. It ships a ZK proof verifier as a native opcode -- Groth16 and RISC Zero STARK verification at L1, the only L1 with native STARK verification. Block headers carry a designated sequencing commitment to application transaction ordering, enabling ZK-enforced based-apps.

#### Silverscript

Silverscript is a compiler for writing covenant logic on Kaspa. It takes covenant logic written in high-level language and compiles it down to Kaspa Script. v1.0.0 is tagged and live. [Silverscript GitHub](https://github.com/kaspanet/silverscript/)

* * *

### DAGKnight hardfork

DAGKnight is the consensus protocol upgrade that follows Toccata. It is a major leap for proof of work and for permissionless consensus: the only 49% BFT partially synchronous protocol (in the oblivious setup). It is a step toward netsplit-resilient proof of work. Block times are targeted for the 40-25 millisecond range. [DAGKnight paper](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1494.pdf)

* * *

### 2027 hardfork

10 millisecond block time - 100 blocks per second - would likely require DAG algorithmic adjustments to how miners reference DAG tips, alongside further node performance optimizations. Targeted for a 2027 hardfork.

On the consensus side, DAGKnight already provides safety under netsplits: transactions confirmed before a split remain final. But it does not provide progress during a split - transactions cannot actually be confirmed until the split is over. The 2027 work aims to add practical progress through a combination of on-chain payment channels and hashrate-adaptive finality windows. This would make Kaspa wargrade hard money, with local payment flows surviving broken internet conditions.

* * *

Kaspa did not come out of the usual hype cycle. It came out of veteran research, fair launch, open-source execution, and years of pushing where most of crypto stopped pushing.

A live blockDAG. 10 BPS on mainnet. Real-time decentralization as the north star. Toccata live. DAGKnight next.

If this reads like it's early, that's because it is.

---

# Build on Kaspa

Mainnet programmability, WASM SDK, native Rust libraries, and node infrastructure for building on Kaspa.

[Open docs](https://docs.kaspa.org/) [View on GitHub](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa)

Fastest way in

## Start building

Start with the docs, live examples, or node route that matches what you need.

Try live

## Run the Rusty Kaspa browser examples

The examples below are served from the Rusty Kaspa v2.0.0 browser SDK release, so you can see the SDK behave without leaving the page.

### Get server info

Connect through the public resolver and fetch basic node information directly from the browser.

[Open standalone](https://kaspa.org/vendor/kaspa-wasm/2.0.0/examples/web/get-server-info.html?returnTo=%2Fbuild%23try-live)[View source](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/v2.0.0/wasm/examples/web/get-server-info.html)

Runs against the [Public Node Network](https://kaspa.aspectron.org/rpc/pnn.html), a decentralized pool of community-operated nodes fronted by the Kaspa Resolver. May take a few seconds to initialize, and is not recommended for large-scale production use.

Paths

## Choose your path

Choose an integration stack, node setup, or programmability model for the system you're building.

App SDK

### Build with the WASM SDK

Use the upstream browser and Node.js bindings for wallet flows, transactions, and RPC access.

[WASM SDK docs](https://kaspa.aspectron.org/docs/)[Upstream examples](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/tree/v2.0.0/wasm/examples)

Native Rust

### Build with native Rust

Use the Rust crates inside Rusty Kaspa for backend services, systems integrations, wallet internals, and node-adjacent workloads.

[Rusty Kaspa repo](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa)

Programmable apps

### Build programmable apps

Compare Covenants, Based Apps, and specialist Inline ZK. Full vProgs remain the future direction for composition between independent apps.

[Choose a model](https://docs.kaspa.org/programmability)[Toccata developer guide](https://docs.kaspa.org/toccata)

Node

### Run a node

Use Rusty Kaspa for full access, UTXO indexing, and production infrastructure.

[Latest release](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/releases/tag/v2.0.1)[Rusty Kaspa repo](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa)

Community APIFor quick reads or constrained environments, a community-hosted API is available. Best-effort, no SLA.

[REST API docs](https://api.kaspa.org/docs)

Node

## Run a node

Spin up Rusty Kaspa locally with Docker. For a persistent setup, check Docker Hub or build from source.

Docker quickstart

### Run the latest Rusty Kaspa image

Exposes gRPC on port 16110 so you can talk to the node from your dev machine. Ephemeral container — no persistent storage or inbound P2P.

```
docker run -d --name kaspad -p 16110:16110 kaspanet/rusty-kaspad:latest
```

[Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/kaspanet/rusty-kaspad)[Compile from source](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa)

Docs, query surfaces, node references, and test flows grouped by what builders actually need.

Query the network through public tools and the lightweight community-hosted API. The community API is best-effort with no SLA.

[Community API docs](https://api.kaspa.org/docs)[Explorer](https://kaspa.stream/)[DAG visualizer](https://kgi.kaspad.net/)[Explorer / API DB dumps](https://db-dl.kaspa.org/)

Community

### Kas Smiths: builders' workshop

Discuss and refine Kaspa standards, protocols, tooling, shared infrastructure, and product ideas with other builders.

](https://kas-smiths.org/)

[

Live on mainnet

### Toccata programmability

Toccata added programmable UTXOs to Kaspa through covenants, transaction introspection, ZK verification, and sequencing support for based apps. It has been live on mainnet since June 30, 2026.

](https://docs.kaspa.org/toccata)

[

Covenant tooling

### Silverscript

The primary higher-level authoring path for mainnet covenants, compiling to native Kaspa Script. Tooling is still early; check current release and audit status before production use.

](https://github.com/kaspanet/silverscript)

[

In construction

### vProgs: Based Apps

The shared-state application path is under construction. The vProgs runtime is an evolving source of patterns, not yet a stable external developer API; Full vProgs remain a future direction.

](https://docs.kaspa.org/programmability/based-apps)

[

SDK

### Python SDK

In beta and nearly complete. Python tooling is progressing in the open and expanding the developer surface.

](https://github.com/kaspanet/kaspa-python-sdk)

[

Protocol

### KIPs

Track proposals that can change how applications and infrastructure integrate with the network.

](https://github.com/kaspanet/kips)

# HODL Kaspa

Buy KAS and move it into a wallet you control.

1

## Get a wallet

## Get a wallet

Choose a wallet that fits how you plan to hold and use KAS.

Step 1 of 4

1

2

3

4

### What is your operating system?

This filters the list to wallets that run on your OS.

Mobile wallets

+Portable and convenient; ideal when making transactions face-to-face

+Designed to use QR codes to make quick and seamless transactions

\-App marketplaces can delist/remove wallets, making future updates harder to receive

\-Damage or loss of the device can potentially lead to loss of funds

Pros and cons

+Portable and convenient; ideal when making transactions face-to-face

+Designed to use QR codes to make quick and seamless transactions

\-App marketplaces can delist/remove wallets, making future updates harder to receive

\-Damage or loss of the device can potentially lead to loss of funds

Desktop wallets

+Desktop environments can give users complete control over funds

+Some desktop wallets offer hardware wallet support or full-node operation

\-Less convenient for QR-code payments when making transactions in person

\-Compromised computers may expose users to malware, spyware, or viruses

Pros and cons

+Desktop environments can give users complete control over funds

+Some desktop wallets offer hardware wallet support or full-node operation

\-Less convenient for QR-code payments when making transactions in person

\-Compromised computers may expose users to malware, spyware, or viruses

Hardware wallets

+One of the most secure methods to store funds

+Ideal for storing large amounts of KAS long-term

\-Less convenient while mobile and not designed for quick transactions

\-Loss of device without proper backup can make funds unrecoverable

Pros and cons

+One of the most secure methods to store funds

+Ideal for storing large amounts of KAS long-term

\-Less convenient while mobile and not designed for quick transactions

\-Loss of device without proper backup can make funds unrecoverable

Missing a wallet? [Learn how to submit it on GitHub](https://github.com/kaspamedia/kaspa-org/blob/main/docs/wallet-submissions.md)

**Important:** Back up your recovery phrase or wallet instructions before moving meaningful funds. Send a small test transaction first, then move the rest only after it arrives.

2

## Buy KAS

## Buy KAS

KAS is listed on many exchanges. Acquire it on a platform supported in your region, then transfer it to your private wallet.

[Kraken](https://www.kraken.com/learn/buy-kaspa-kas)[KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/how-to-buy/kaspa)[MEXC](https://www.mexc.com/how-to-buy/KAS)[CoinEx](https://www.coinex.com/s/buy-kaspa)[Bybit](https://www.bybit.com/en/how-to-buy/kaspa/)[Gate](https://www.gate.io/how-to-buy/kaspa)[BingX](https://bingx.com/en-us/how-to-buy/kaspa/)[Bitget](https://www.bitget.com/how-to-buy/kaspa)[WEEX](https://www.weex.com/pl/futures/KAS-USDT)[BitMart](https://www.bitmart.com/trade/KAS_USDT)[OurBit](https://www.ourbit.com/exchange/KAS_USDT?_from=market)[BYDFi](https://www.bydfi.com/en/spot/kas_usdt)[LBank](https://www.lbank.info/trade/kas_usdt)[CoinW](https://www.coinw.com/spot/kasusdt)

And 50+ more

3

## Take custody of your KAS

## Take custody of your KAS

Secure your assets by transferring them from the exchange to your private wallet.

Receive

kaspa:qrge...3a2w

Step 01

### Get your receive address

Open your Kaspium app, tap 'Receive', and copy your unique address.

Step 02

### Send a test transaction

Withdraw a tiny fraction of KAS from the exchange to verify the route is correct.

Step 03

### Transfer the balance

Once the test transaction arrives safely in your wallet, withdraw the remaining balance.

**Exchange wait times:** Native Kaspa transfers are practically instant, but exchanges apply their own internal delays. It is completely normal to wait 30–60 minutes for an exchange to release your funds to the network.

**Security Check:** Always verify the first and last few characters of your address before confirming.
